title: fix(ci): restore green workflow baseline
body:
## Updated Instagram blocker — verified Meta response (September 15, 2026)

This supersedes the earlier uncertainty between an outage and inspector configuration.

The attached browser shows a response from Meta Support in [case 1978991836117141](https://developers.facebook.com/support/bugs/1978991836117141/). Meta states that Facebook Graph `/debug_token` does not reliably support Instagram Login tokens, including dashboard-generated tokens; changing the authenticating app/credential combination will not resolve that limitation. Meta reports no documented read-only API with equivalent introspection and recommends its [Access Token Debugger portal](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/accesstoken/) for manual inspection. The case is marked closed. This is Meta's stated limitation, not proof of a platform-wide outage.

Consequently, the existing failure is classified as an **unsupported provider validation path**. Repository secret-name/update metadata is unchanged; no credential value was accessed. The original run remains failed: [34922343353](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34922343353). It was not rerun, and its ownership/expiry gate was not removed or treated as successful based only on `/me`.

Next step requires an explicitly approved validation/lifecycle design: inspect the current credential privately through Meta's portal, or authorize a supported reauthorization/exchange/refresh workflow with securely bound provenance and provider-returned lifecycle evidence. A working-account response alone cannot replace ownership and expiry validation. No token refresh, reauthorization, secret replacement, deployment, new attestation, or weaker check was performed.

GitHub access and the repository preflight were reverified; preflight has no errors (only absent daily memory notes). Main remains `73edd77a36c8dcc73e5217303c62376ae684853b`. PR #331 remains `25416b43eb8a24b2a57a180fbb846d9db8addcb1`, open/draft/mergeable with 17 successful checks and no auto-merge. The earlier full-local UI failure and human-review requirements remain disclosed.


---

## CI reconciliation follow-up — September 15, 2026

This updates the earlier CI audit; it does not change the payment-provider activation boundary.

- Initial audit main: `17a33eca11d585d84435af85340beece9b51d14e`.
- Current main: `73edd77a36c8dcc73e5217303c62376ae684853b`.

It is open, draft, mergeable/conflict-free, with auto-merge off. Its 17 reported checks are successful. It still requires a fresh human approval and the author's draft/readiness decision.
- Latest inventory: 36 open PRs; only #331 was present in the initial scope. Later PRs were not rewritten.

### Integration root causes and changes

Main's merge made #331 conflict with the corrected baseline. The resolution preserves reaction locking/privacy/legacy evidence, durable per-party onboarding recovery above public routes, payment-provider fail-closed controls, and lazy route/analytics splitting.

The authoritative migration manifest's automatic merge duplicated two entries and omitted contextual reputation. A uniqueness regression reproduced 104 unique IDs in 106 entries. The corrected manifest contains the exact 102 ordered main entries plus three payment migrations: 105 total, with no changed SQL or historical checksums. Three additional prerequisite-order assertions protect reputation, payment-intent synchronization and provider capability setup.

While integration was being validated, another actor pushed equivalent application/migration reconciliation in `e39abf5a4ce2151e03dbd91051ba508295081efb`. Our first normal push was safely rejected. We compared the resulting trees, retained that published commit, and appended only:
- `scripts/__tests__/production-release.test.mjs`: three migration-order assertions.
- `tdf-hq-ui/src/pages/LoginPage.test.tsx`: explicitly advance the real MUI dialog exit timers inside awaited React act, restoring real timers afterward; retain the assertion that the dialog is absent.

This fixes the dismissal test's wall-clock animation race without increasing timeouts, changing application behavior or reducing coverage. No force-push or contributor-history rewrite occurred.

Generated clients remain authoritative and reproducible in both consumers: SHA-256 `c77b987df160bab0c719a17b850a8df27f5da3bab9decabe8772a84b8644bc4a`. Existing mobile commit `c1ae3e34b53f8e709d361677d20b9778bdf87d61` is retained; no additional mobile commit was needed. Catalog integration preserved all 947 main manual decisions unchanged, retained three individually inspected PR-specific decisions and 161 policy decisions; stale IDs were removed, not bulk approved.

### Validation and honest local limitations

- Fresh final-SHA CI: UI 207 suites / 1,971 tests; mobile 68 / 329; backend 2,546 examples / zero failures; persona 46 passed / 10 legitimate deduplication skips. All contract, migration, runtime, dependency/security-policy, lint, type, build and aggregate gates passed. The separately dispatched final-SHA image workflow also passed every job.
- Local integrated tree `1ef240b082a7b774ad2a371a4d5013ed15edf96d`, equivalent in application/test content to the preserved published resolution plus follow-up: complete `REQUIRE_STACK=1 REQUIRE_MOBILE_WORKSPACE=1 npm exec --offline --yes --package=node@22.14.0 -- npm run quality` exited 0. UI 207/1,971; mobile 68/329; backend 2,546; production initial bundle 5 preloads / 314,734 gzip bytes. This is not mislabeled as final-SHA execution.
- Final-SHA repetition of that complete local command exited 1: repo checks, UI lint/types passed; UI 202 suites / 1,964 tests passed and 5 suites / 7 tests failed in 2,012.9 seconds. Failures begin with unchanged five-second watchdogs in MerchAdminPage, ArtistPublicPage, publicRoutes and ForbiddenPage, plus a MarketplaceOrderTracking loading-state cascade. Host memory pressure was directly observed. No process was terminated and no test limit was increased. This repetition is not green and the later local build/mobile/backend stages did not execute.
- One isolated diagnostic run of those five files passed all 5 suites / 14 tests in 17.98 seconds, without any source, timeout or assertion change. This supports the resource-contention diagnosis, not a reclassification of the failed complete run. No repeated full-suite rerun-to-green was used.
- Final image digest: `sha256:8ca18af9208eea1d6b646c933ecfd887f5230e1353d870b8aaaf082a2225882b`, published only under the immutable final commit tag.
- Final focused production-release tests: 53 passed; strict catalog audit exited 0 for all 1,111 candidates; generated clients show no drift; `git diff --check` passed and the worktree is clean.
- Separate final-SHA `npm run build --workspace=tdf-hq-ui` exited 0: production build and unchanged initial-bundle gate passed (5 preloads / 314,737 gzip bytes). The pre-existing large-chunk warning remains disclosed; no limit was raised.
- Separate final-SHA `REQUIRE_MOBILE_WORKSPACE=1 npm exec --offline --yes --package=node@22.14.0 -- npm run quality:mobile` exited 0: lint, types, 68 suites / 329 tests passed (50.507 seconds for tests).
- Separate final-SHA `REQUIRE_STACK=1 npm exec --offline --yes --package=node@22.14.0 -- npm run quality:backend` exited 0: 2,546 examples, zero failures (8.3815 seconds for tests).
- Docker migration harness could not start its disposable PostgreSQL service within its startup window, before any SQL assertion. A native PostgreSQL 16.10 equivalent preserved the original assertion body verbatim, replacing only isolated database setup/psql adapters; it passed apply/reapply, disabled-provider defaults, invalid-activation rejection, intent binding, immutable references, balanced commissions, dual-control payout and evidence-preserving rollback refusal. Its own temporary database was cleaned up. The failed Docker startup is not reported as a passed Docker run.

### Expected skips, security and rollback

The 10 persona skips deduplicate mutation-heavy journeys across browser projects. Ordinary PR CI does not publish the backend executable; its upload step is legitimately skipped. Build Image requests the artifact and successfully uploads/downloads it. Manual enrichment uses the non-publishing dry-run branch and skips its mutually exclusive scheduled branch. Success-only runs omit failure notifications. Datadog's missing-key fallback skips because the real test step executes. No unexpected job skips occurred in final CI or image build.

Datadog is verified as TDF Records / US1. Existing repository `DD_API_KEY` and `DD_APP_KEY` are configured; no secret values were read, copied or rotated by this agent. Its two production endpoint tests verify deployed liveness, not this PR's deployment or actual database connectivity. No paid plan or recurring test schedule was enabled.

The published follow-up is test-only. Existing additive payment migrations keep providers disabled. No provider activation, credential rotation, live transaction, production migration or deployment was performed. Historical ledger/checksum/evidence rows remain immutable; rollback must refuse erasure after financial evidence exists and use a reviewed roll-forward instead. Existing dependency advisory exceptions remain unchanged; passing the repository security policy is not a zero-advisory claim.

### Remaining actions / status boundary

1. **Meta blocker:** workflow Refresh Instagram Token, step Check/Refresh Token, repository-scoped `FACEBOOK_APP_ID`/`FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET` (parent debugger) and separate `INSTAGRAM_APP_ID`/`INSTAGRAM_APP_SECRET`/`INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN`. Account access works; debug_token returns HTTP 400 / code 2, service temporarily unavailable. A platform-wide outage is not proven. The app administrator must verify the TDF Bot / TDF Bot-IG inspector association and investigate with Meta if needed; do not blindly rotate keys. Then use existing `action=check` and require account, ownership and expiry validation to succeed. Optional `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` is absent; notification omission does not hide the primary failure.
2. **Local environment:** complete a final-SHA full local suite in an adequately resourced environment. Fresh hosted CI and image build are green, but the final local repetition is not.
3. **Human review:** #331 remains draft with no effective fresh approval; the repository requires one approval and dismisses stale reviews. No protections, draft state, approvals or merge controls were bypassed.
4. **Original handoff:** #333 cannot be delivered as an open correction PR because another actor already merged it. Its fixes are now on main; this approved continuation repaired the originally scoped #331 without creating an extra correction PR.

Verified final PR CI/image results, current-main workflow results, older-SHA scheduled evidence, local limitations and the Meta blocker are deliberately distinguished. The repository-wide objective is not claimed fully green.

## Historical original-correction audit

The following is the earlier PR #333 description, preserved for its original root causes, regression evidence and review history. Main-build, scheduled-check and PR #331 conflict/readiness statements from the earlier snapshot are superseded by the follow-up above.

The latest refreshed inventory contains 31 open PRs and no longer includes merged PR #333; PR #331 is the only originally open PR in scope and still has 17 successful checks.

## Root causes and implementation

Classification: migration ordering, generated-client drift, Haskell typing, stale UI contract assumptions, catalog decisions and shell exit masking were deterministic application/configuration defects. Persona instability came from the shared development-preview configuration; the oversized provider-title test had a test-isolation/watchdog defect. The aggregate quality and image gates were downstream failures, not separate defects. MusicBrainz failures are external transients handled by bounded retries and evidence-preserving withholding. The remaining Meta metadata error is an external-service or account-configuration requirement, with the exact upstream cause not yet established. Earlier local-only watchdog cascades occurred under heavy host contention and are reported separately from fresh CI.

1. **Migration batch:** restored prerequisite order, missing September entries, immutable checksums, and uniqueness in the authoritative 102-entry manifest. Replay, compatibility, preflight, and checksum-rejection coverage remain enforced.
2. **Generated clients:** regenerated both consumers from authoritative OpenAPI with the declared toolchain and verified reproducibility. Published mobile submodule commit: `790e03e1fb19083a92c2828a8b77ba1016fd53e4`.
3. **Onboarding/UI:** replaced obsolete client-only completion with server-authoritative, party-scoped, durable and idempotent recovery. Recovery now mounts above public and protected routes and retries on reconnect. Account-switch guards and explicit review before directory-contact replay remain intact.
4. **Moment reactions:** corrected optional DTO typing; serialized mutations by locking the moment before lookup; emitted durable engagement evidence transactionally. Only the caller's reaction exposes identity/time. Legacy active reactions repair missing evidence once, using their original creation timestamp rather than fabricating a new action time.
5. **Persona journeys:** production preview replaces concurrent development workers that invalidated dependency hashes. Browser/device coverage and assertions remain unchanged.
6. **Catalog authority:** evidence-backed reconciliation preserves manual review, refreshes deterministic policy decisions, removes stale IDs, and records sources. The reviewed result is 1,108 candidates/decisions with zero stale or unreviewed records—not blanket approval.
7. **Enrichment:** bounded retries, jitter, Retry-After handling, timeouts and redacted outage classification distinguish transient provider failures from corrupt data. Unverifiable changes are withheld. Both research paths suppress false “no exact match” attribution for unavailable providers. Permanent authentication/data-integrity failures still fail.
8. **CI integrity:** safe-install exits propagate. Datadog explicitly targets TDF Records/US1, fails on critical errors or missing tests, uses a read-only GitHub token, and keeps API/application keys away from checkout and unrelated steps. No test/matrix/trigger/threshold was removed or weakened.
9. **Account-switch recovery:** preserve dismissal/failure state per party so late failures remain recoverable without overwriting the active party's state. Two regressions reproduced the original missing-guidance/error behavior and passed after the fix; another local isolated run encountered watchdog/cascade failures. Lint, type checking and the strict 1,108-decision catalog audit passed locally; final-SHA UI CI passed the entire onboarding file and all 1,968 tests.
10. **UI test isolation:** each provider-title input now has its own test boundary and cleanup. This retains all 101 inputs and assertions and prevents a single large matrix from exhausting one shared watchdog.
11. **Token maintenance:** invalid responses fail closed; read-only Instagram account validation precedes metadata checks; permanent auth failures do not retry. The Facebook debugger uses the associated parent Meta application's credentials separately from Instagram Login credentials; returned app ownership, explicit expiration, and data-access deadlines are checked. CI caught missing application query-field imports, then a missing `selectList` import in the regression test; both were corrected. The prior CI/build failures on `64fd4c82c` were deterministic compiler failures, not rerun as flakes. Token material is not logged, Fly commands avoid shell interpolation, and update/restart failures propagate. Slack credentials are scoped only to the configuration/notification steps.

## Datadog setup and evidence

The signed-in organization is **TDF Records**, site **US1** (`app.datadoghq.com`; action setting `datadoghq.com`). Repository secret-name/update metadata confirms `DD_API_KEY` and `DD_APP_KEY` are now configured; this agent did not read, copy, or rotate their values.

- Main also has a directly verified substantive [Datadog rerun](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34554413898), attempt 2: two passed, zero failures/skips/missing tests. This does not make main's unrelated failing workflows green.
- Both were discovered by the existing `tag:e2e-tests` query and passed from São Paulo (AWS) in the [final batch](https://app.datadoghq.com/synthetics/explorer/ci?batchResultId=ea9f97fe-68f6-4194-94f4-42d6ff3034a6).
- These validate deployed production endpoints, not the unmerged PR deployment. The PR's independent persona/contract/integration suites remain required. No duplicate test draft was saved, billing plan upgraded, or recurring schedule enabled by this agent.

## Validation and limitations

- Lockfile-based root/mobile installs, double API generation, strict catalog audit, PostgreSQL 17 authoritative batch replay and rollback-compatibility checks passed during correction development. Generated-client SHA-256: `e230e1db74bb789c969a284a4eec6464f8577d7305a1af4be58419758635f54e`.

- Focused CI/token tests: 26 passed; provider-enrichment tests on final source: 21 passed; public-route recovery/onboarding tests: 18 passed.
- Full local UI on preceding `b246a8fb8`: lint and type checking passed; full tests finished with 201 suites passing, 5 failing, 1,953 tests passing and 14 failing in 1,927.9 seconds. Failures involved CourseBuilder, Marketplace, registration sorting, Logs, and RefundManagementPanel, beginning with timeouts and followed by React cleanup/assertion cascades. The one isolated diagnostic run passed 29/30 tests (four suites); registration sorting still hit its unchanged five-second timeout. An exploratory React test-environment/cleanup change also timed out and was removed; it is not part of the PR. This full local run is **not passing**.
